key_concepts.concept: Basketball offense is a perception-action skill: the player must see defender position, teammate spacing, basket location, clock context, and help rotations while executing technique.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Progress from isolated form work to tasks with targets, time limits, defenders, advantage-disadvantage constraints, and pass-dribble-shoot choices.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English
Training load and match-play demands in basketball based on competition level: A systematic review

key_concepts.concept: Ready stance, balance, stopping, pivoting, and efficient footwork are the base of shooting, passing, driving, screening, and finishing.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Teach every skill from an athletic base: eyes up, hips loaded, feet active, torso controlled, and the ball protected in a position that can become a pass, shot, or drive.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Triple threat is not a static pose; it is a balanced catch position from which the player can shoot, pass, rip, jab, pivot, or drive without telegraphing.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Reward quick catch-ready feet, eyes on rim, ball protection, and a first action based on the defender's closeout rather than a pre-planned move.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: A dribble should improve the offense: beat a defender, create a passing angle, escape pressure, improve spacing, or enter an action.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Use dribble limits, advantage games, and live reads so players learn when not to dribble as much as how to dribble.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Effective ball handlers separate with rhythm disruption: slow-fast, high-low body level, hesitation, retreat, stop-start, and then directional change.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Teach moves with a setup, speed change, shoulder/hip deception, low hard transfer, and acceleration for two steps after the move.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Passing can shift the defense faster than the ball handler can dribble, but only when the passer reads the receiver, defender, timing, and pass window.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Train pass type, pass timing, receiver movement, target hands, and next action together instead of only stationary partner passing.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Shooting accuracy depends on repeatable lower-body loading, stable balance, ball path, elbow and wrist organization, guide-hand control, release angle, arc, and follow-through.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Start close enough that the player can keep the same motion, then extend range only when mechanics stay stable under fatigue, movement, and contest.
source_refs: 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics
Biomechanical Analysis of the Jump Shot in Basketball

key_concepts.concept: Free throws are performed without defender pressure but under fatigue, score pressure, and self-regulation demands, so routine and movement consistency matter.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Build a short routine, consistent breathing, stable stance, one target focus, and controlled knee and center-of-mass rhythm; avoid changing mechanics during pressure sets.
source_refs: Biomechanical characteristics of proficient free-throw shooters

key_concepts.concept: Catch-and-shoot quality is created by off-ball readiness: relocation, hands ready, feet organized before or during the catch, eyes to the rim, and quick shot preparation.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Coach the preparatory hop or 1-2 step, catch pocket, shoulders to rim, and immediate decision to shoot, drive a closeout, or swing.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Off-dribble shooting requires the player to decelerate, gather, align feet and shoulders, transfer the ball cleanly from dribble to shot pocket, and release before the defender recovers.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Train pickup timing, one-two and hop gathers, inside-foot stops, balance after separation, and contested release windows.
source_refs: Biomechanical Adjustments of the Basketball Jump Shot Performed Over Opponents of Different Height
High-Intensity Acceleration and Deceleration Demands in Elite Team Sports Competitive Match Play

key_concepts.concept: Rim finishing combines approach angle, gather footwork, takeoff choice, ball protection, body control, touch, backboard use, and reading the shot blocker.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Teach same-foot and opposite-foot finishes, outside-hand layups, stride stops, jump stops, floaters, inside-hand finishes, and pass-out reads against help.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Spacing is maintained by all five offensive players through width, depth, corner occupation, slot balance, dunker or short-corner use, and timely replacement after drives or cuts.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Use small-sided games to teach lift, drift, fill, replace, cut-through, and exit spacing when the ball drives or a screen is used.

key_concepts.concept: A screen creates advantage only when the screener arrives with legal body position, the cutter or handler uses the screen shoulder-to-shoulder, and the off-ball players preserve passing lanes.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Teach screen angle, stationary contact point, waiting for the screen, rubbing the defender, and then rolling, popping, slipping, or rescreening based on coverage.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

key_concepts.concept: Pick-and-roll is not only a two-player action; the handler, screener, corner, slot, and weak-side players all affect the tag, stunt, roll lane, kickout, and second-side attack.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Progress from 2-on-0 timing to 2-on-2 reads, then 3-on-3 with a corner spacer, then 4-on-4 or 5-on-5 with tag and rotation decisions.

key_concepts.concept: 1-on-1, 2-on-2, 3-on-3, and constraint games produce more touches, more spacing decisions, and clearer feedback than full 5-on-5 repetition for developing players.
key_concepts.coaching_application: Use constraints such as two-dribble max, no-dribble, score after a paint touch, score after a cut, or advantage starts to connect technique to tactical decisions.

components: Athletic stance with hips low enough to change direction.
Eyes available to read floor, not fixed on the ball.
Finger-pad control with relaxed hand and variable dribble height.
Ball protected outside the defender's reach with body, arm bar, and angle.
Moves connected to an outcome: pass, drive, shot, escape, or enter offense.
beginner_progression: Stationary pound dribbles with both hands.
Stationary height changes: ankle, knee, waist.
Walking dribble with eyes up and target calls.
Cone or line dribble with stop and pivot.
intermediate_progression: Retreat dribble into crossover, between-the-legs, or behind-the-back.
Change-of-pace dribble into two-step acceleration.
1-on-1 from wing with two-dribble limit.
Pressure escape to pass or attack.
advanced_progression: Live ball-screen setup and snake dribble reads.
Split, reject, hostage, and retreat reads against coverage.
Late-clock isolation with help defenders.
Full-court pressure handling with pass-ahead decisions.

common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Add visual calls, colored cones, numbered fingers, or passing targets that require head-up information.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Change-of-direction move is wide and slow.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Cue low hard transfer, outside-foot push, hip drop, and two fast steps after the move.
Use dribble limits and score only after paint touch, pass advantage, or open shot creation.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Ball is exposed to the defender.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Teach body between ball and defender, outside-hand dribble, and chin-shoulder checks before exposing the ball.

technical_models.model: See the advantage, create the window, pass on time, catch ready, continue the action.
pass_families: Two-hand chest pass for direct open lanes.
Bounce pass for defender hands high or pocket-feed windows.
Overhead pass for size, outlet, skip, and post-entry angles.
One-hand push pass for drive-and-kick or off-dribble passing.
Hook, wrap, pocket, lob, and drift passes for advanced pick-and-roll or help reads.
receiver_responsibilities: Step toward or move to the pass line.
Catch with balance and eyes to rim.
Convert immediately to shot, pass, drive, or pivot.
beginner_progression: Stationary partner chest and bounce passing with target hands.
Wall passing to targets with step and backspin.
Pass and follow, pass and cut, pass and replace.
Three-player passing with no defense.
intermediate_progression: Passing on the move with layup or catch-and-shoot finish.
Drive-and-kick with corner and slot receivers.
Post entry from wing with defender fronting or behind.
Advantage 3-on-2 and 4-on-3 decisions.
advanced_progression: Pick-and-roll reads: pocket, hit-ahead, skip, lift, drift, and short-roll pass.
Passing against traps with pivot, fake, and split vision.
Second-side reversal after paint touch.
Late-clock passing with shot-quality decision rules.

common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Cue step to target, firm wrist snap, shorter passing window, and earlier decision from the catch.
Require receiver to show hands, step to ball, or move into a passing lane before the pass can be made.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Player predetermines pass into covered lane.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Add live defender with score for deflections and coach passer to read defender chest and hand position.
Teach jump passes only as advanced emergency actions; emphasize pivoting, pass fakes, and landing on two before passing.

components: Balanced feet with knees and hips loaded.
Shooting-side alignment through foot, knee, hip, shoulder, elbow, hand, and eye as much as anatomy allows.
Ball moves to shot pocket without unnecessary drift.
Shooting elbow organized under or slightly inside the ball.
Guide hand stabilizes but does not push.
Legs and trunk transfer force smoothly into arm extension.
Release has relaxed wrist snap, backspin, and held follow-through.
shot_contexts: Step-back or side-step only after base mechanics are stable.
beginner_progression: One-hand form shooting near basket.
Add guide hand without guide-hand push.
Set shot from short range.
Free throw routine with stable stance.
intermediate_progression: 1-2 and hop footwork catch-and-shoot.
Relocation shooting from corner, wing, and slot.
One-dribble pull-up going both directions.
Shot fake to one-dribble shot or pass.
advanced_progression: Movement shooting from pin-down, flare, drift, lift, and transition trails.
Off-dribble shooting after change of pace, ball screen, or retreat.
Contested shooting with late closeout.
Fatigue and score-pressure shooting sets.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Range is too far and mechanics collapse.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Move closer until arc, elbow path, and follow-through are repeatable; extend only after makes with stable form.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Guide hand pushes or twists the ball.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Use one-hand form shooting, guide-hand freeze, and check that guide fingers finish quiet to the side.
Cue feet and hands ready before the pass, then use hop or inside-foot 1-2 into a balanced base.
Train deceleration, gather under hips, shoulders to rim, and vertical landing after release.

components: Same pre-shot routine every repetition.
Balanced stance and relaxed shoulders.
Controlled knee bend and center-of-mass rhythm.
Stable gaze on a precise target.
Smooth release with follow-through held until the ball reaches the rim.
training_progression: Blocked free throws for routine learning.
Free throws after sprint, defensive slide, or contact finish.
Game-scenario sets by score and clock.

common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Track process adherence separately from makes and require the same routine after make or miss.
Use breath count and a fixed cue word before the shooting motion starts.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Excessive knee or trunk motion changes release.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Use video from side and front to stabilize rhythm and release timing.

technical_models.model: Get paint advantage, gather under control, protect the ball, choose finish, land ready.
finish_families: Inside-hand layup to shield from shot blocker.
Power layup off jump stop or stride stop.
Reverse finish using rim as protection.
Floater or runner before the shot blocker can contest.
Euro, pro-hop, spin, or stride variation after fundamentals are stable.
Pass-out to corner, dunker spot, or lift when help commits.
beginner_progression: No-dribble one-step and two-step layup footwork.
Mikan-style alternating finishes close to rim.
Dribble from wing into outside-hand layup.
Stride-stop layup after pass or cut.
intermediate_progression: Finishing through pad contact.
Inside-hand and reverse layups.
Floater off one foot and two feet.
1-on-1 from advantage start with help defender.
advanced_progression: Ball-screen downhill finishes against drop, switch, and late help.
Paint decision games: finish, lob, drift pass, kickout, or short pass.
Contested rim reads with verticality and shot blocker timing.
Transition finishing at speed with trailing defender.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Player gathers too early and gets blocked.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Teach long first step, late pickup, ball outside frame, and alternate finish angles.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Player avoids contact and drifts away from rim.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Train shoulder-to-chest line, two-foot power gathers, and controlled contact pads before live defense.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Layup footwork is reversed or causes travels.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Return to slow one-step and two-step rhythm, then add dribble only after steps are automatic.
Cue soft hand, high release, vertical body, and target above front rim or backboard area depending on angle.

technical_models.model: Stop balanced, protect pivot, threaten rim, move defender, attack advantage.
components: Jump stop and stride stop.
Front pivot and reverse pivot.
Rip-through and sweep below or above defender hands.
Jab step to move defender without losing balance.
Shot fake and drive fake with eyes and body believable.
Inside-foot 1-2 and hop footwork into shot.
beginner_progression: Athletic stance and jump-stop freeze.
Pivot square to basket without traveling.
Triple-threat catch with eyes to rim.
Jab and return to balance.
intermediate_progression: Jab to drive, jab to shot, shot fake to one-dribble pull-up.
Pivot out of pressure and pass.
Catch on wing, read closeout, choose shoot-drive-swing.
Stride stop into pivot and finish.
advanced_progression: Pressure catches with live defender.
Late-clock pivot package.
Post-perimeter hybrid footwork: rip, drop, step-through, fade, pass.
Closeout attack with second defender help read.

common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Call and mark pivot foot, freeze after each move, and add defense only after legal foot discipline holds.

common_errors_and_corrections.error: Jab step makes player stand tall.
common_errors_and_corrections.correction: Cue short violent jab, chest over hips, ball protected, and immediate return to loaded stance.
Require eyes to rim, ball to shot pocket, and same lower-body load as the player's real shot.

tactical_rules.rule: Maintain usable width and depth: corners stretch help, slots create reversal lanes, and one interior or short-corner player can occupy rim protection without clogging drives.
tactical_rules.why_it_matters: Poor spacing lets one defender guard two players, shrinks driving lanes, removes passing angles, and reduces shot quality.
coaching_cues: If you cut through, another player fills behind.
If the ball drives baseline, weak-side players drift or lift to visible windows.
If the ball drives middle, corners stay spaced and slots prepare for kickout or extra pass.
Do not stand in the same vertical lane as a teammate unless screening or cutting with purpose.
progression: 4-on-4 drive-and-kick with drift and lift rules.

tactical_rules.rule: Cut when denied, after passing if the lane is open, or when a defender turns their head; replace when a teammate cuts through.
tactical_rules.why_it_matters: Cutting punishes ball watching, creates layups, opens second-side space, and teaches off-ball players to be active decision-makers.
coaching_cues: Set up the defender before cutting.
Cut hard to score, not just to move.
Clear to opposite side if not open.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

tactical_rules.rule: On the catch, read the closeout: shoot if late and balanced, drive if long or out of control, swing if help is loaded and a teammate has a better advantage.
tactical_rules.why_it_matters: This links triple threat, catch-and-shoot, passing, and driving into one decision instead of isolated skills.
coaching_cues: Eyes to rim on every catch.
Make the decision before the ball sticks.
One hard advantage dribble beats more than three neutral dribbles.
If you draw help, pass on time.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

tactical_rules.rule: The handler creates separation, waits for the screen angle, uses the screen tight, reads the screener's defender, and then scores, hits the roller, kicks to spacing, rejects, or resets.
tactical_rules.why_it_matters: A ball screen only creates advantage when timing, angle, spacing, and coverage reads align.

handler: Set up defender with pace, jab, retreat, or change of angle.
Keep dribble alive until the help decision is clear.
Read drop, switch, hedge, trap, under, and ice-style positioning.
screener: Sprint to screen with legal stationary body position.
Angle the screen to the intended attack lane.
Hold contact long enough for handler to use it.
Roll, pop, slip, or rescreen based on defender behavior.
spacers: Lift, drift, or cut only when it opens the passing lane.

progression: 3-on-3 with corner spacer and tag defender.

tactical_rules.rule: Screens must be legal, timed, and used tightly; the cutter or handler should wait for contact angle before exploding off the screen.
tactical_rules.why_it_matters: Early cuts, moving screens, and wide routes remove the screen advantage and can create turnovers or fouls.
coaching_cues: Screener: sprint, stop, be wide and strong, hands protected.
User: walk defender into screen, shoulder-to-hip path, explode after the screen.
After contact: roll, pop, slip, or re-screen with eyes to the ball.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English

tactical_rules.rule: A paint touch should trigger a scoring decision: finish, pass to dunker or short corner, kick to corner, pass to lift, or spray to second side.
tactical_rules.why_it_matters: The paint touch forces help and creates high-value shots only if teammates maintain passing windows and the handler reads early.
coaching_cues: Do not drive into a crowd without a pass plan.
Weak-side slot lifts if their defender tags the roller.
After kickout, attack the closeout before the defense fully recovers.

physical_demands.quality: Lower-body strength, power, and elastic stiffness support first step, vertical jump, shot range, rebounding into second shots, and finishing through contact.
physical_demands.training_implication: Use age-appropriate jumping, landing, sprinting, strength, and mobility progressions before high-volume advanced shooting or contact finishing.

physical_demands.quality: Basketball offense repeatedly requires stopping from sprints, drives, cuts, and ball-screen attacks.
physical_demands.training_implication: Teach landing mechanics, hip-knee-ankle flexion, trunk control, and progressive braking volume before high-speed pull-ups and aggressive change-of-direction work.
source_refs: Training load and match-play demands in basketball based on competition level: A systematic review
High-Intensity Acceleration and Deceleration Demands in Elite Team Sports Competitive Match Play

physical_demands.quality: Fine motor control, bilateral coordination, timing, and rhythm support dribble control, passing touch, shooting sequence, and finishing variety.
physical_demands.training_implication: Use varied rhythms, both hands, different ball sizes for youth when appropriate, and constraints that force timing changes without overloading intensity.

physical_demands.quality: Trunk control lets players absorb contact, keep shooting line, pivot without travel, pass through pressure, and finish at non-straight angles.
physical_demands.training_implication: Integrate balance, single-leg strength, anti-rotation, landing stability, and contact-control drills into skill work.

physical_demands.quality: Basketball is intermittent and demands repeated high-intensity actions with short recovery.
physical_demands.training_implication: Condition through representative small-sided games, transition sequences, and work-rest intervals rather than only long steady running.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High volumes of stops, cuts, side-steps, pull-ups, and direction changes can overload ankles, knees, hips, and low back, especially if added suddenly.
risk_controls: Teach braking with hip-knee-ankle flexion and trunk control.
Alternate high-speed change-of-direction days with lower-impact skill days.
Monitor soreness, landing quality, and fatigue-related knee valgus or trunk collapse.
source_refs: High-Intensity Acceleration and Deceleration Demands in Elite Team Sports Competitive Match Play
Training load and match-play demands in basketball based on competition level: A systematic review

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High-volume jump shots, contested shooting, layups, and finishing drills add repeated takeoff and landing load.
risk_controls: Build from set shooting to jump shooting to movement shooting.
Control shot-count spikes, especially for youth and return-to-play athletes.
Mix form shooting, free throws, passing, and tactical decision work between high-jump blocks.
source_refs: Biomechanical Analysis of the Jump Shot in Basketball
Epidemiology of Injuries Among National Basketball Association Players

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Contact finishes and screening drills increase collision, shoulder, wrist, rib, hip, knee, and ankle risk if players lack body control or legal screening technique.
risk_controls: Teach legal stationary screens and safe angles.
Pair players by size and readiness.
Stop drills when contact quality becomes reckless.
source_refs: WABC Level 1 Coaches Course Manual - English
Epidemiology of Injuries Among National Basketball Association Players

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Young players who shoot from regulation three-point range before strength and mechanics are ready often develop compensations such as heaving, low release, guide-hand push, or excessive trunk motion.
risk_controls: Use age-appropriate ball size and basket height when available.
Prioritize close-range form and free throws before long-range volume.
Move players closer when mechanics degrade.
Avoid making deep shooting the main marker of youth offensive value.
source_refs: WABC Mini Basketball Coaches Manual - English
7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

training_implications.principle: Teach mechanics clearly, then quickly add perception, timing, defense, and scoring context.
example_session_flow: Decision drill with one defender or coach cue.
Small-sided live game with a constraint.
Short reflection on decision quality, not only makes.

training_implications.principle: Constraints such as no dribble, two dribbles, mandatory paint touch, score after cut, or bonus for extra pass teach players why and when skills matter.
examples: 3-on-3 no dribble to teach cutting, spacing, and passing.
1-on-1 two dribbles to teach efficient first step and shot quality.
4-on-3 advantage to teach pass timing and help reads.
Pick-and-roll 3-on-3 with corner spacer to teach tag and kickout.

training_implications.principle: Do not overload a developing player with five cues at once; pick the highest-leverage correction for the current skill.
examples: For shooting, focus on base and guide hand before contested range.
For dribbling, focus on eyes up and change of pace before advanced move variety.
For finishing, focus on legal gather and ball protection before acrobatic finishes.

training_implications.principle: Offensive players need both hands and multiple approach angles because defenses remove preferred options.
examples: Left and right hand layups from both sides.
Passing off either foot and either hand after penetration.

training_implications.principle: Track more than makes: footwork legality, decision speed, paint touches, open-shot rate, turnover rate, pass timing, and repeatable mechanics.
examples: Chart catch-and-shoot attempts where feet and hands were ready.
Score pick-and-roll reps by correct read before scoring outcome.
Count turnovers caused by late passing windows.
Track free-throw routine adherence under fatigue.

training_implications.principle: A skill session becomes a physical load session when it includes high-speed changes, jumps, contested finishes, or repeated transition reps.
examples: Alternate shooting blocks with passing or tactical walk-throughs.
Use small-sided games for conditioning but monitor landing and braking quality.
Reduce contact volume when athletes show fatigue or poor control.
